title: [Illustrative] Early TREM2 agonism reduces neuritic dystrophy if TREM2 works
statement: In amyloid-positive brains at an early stage, a TREM2 agonist reduces neuritic dystrophy relative to vehicle when microglial TREM2 is functional, and has no effect when TREM2 function is lost.
mechanism: Agonism enhances TREM2-dependent microglial clustering and plaque compaction, which limits dystrophic neurite formation; without functional receptor the agonist has nothing to act on.
predictions: Early stage, TREM2-normal: agonist reduces dystrophy vs vehicle.
Early stage, TREM2 loss-of-function: no change vs vehicle.

experiments.design: Amyloid-positive mouse model, TREM2-normal and TREM2 loss-of-function arms, early and late stage, agonist antibody vs vehicle.
experiments.readout: Neuritic dystrophy (LAMP1+ dystrophic neurites per plaque) relative to vehicle.

evidence.note: Illustrative demo hypothesis. No literature was consulted and none is claimed; the formal check never reads this field.
